detaileddescription.para: The timer plugin allows measuring time spent by PDI and its plugins.

Each timer records the time spent between a start and a stop event, accumulated over all the times it is started and stopped. When the plugin is unloaded, it outputs the time accumulated by each timer that was started at least once.

sect1.title: Example of a Timer configuration
sect1.para: In this example, timer_B is equivalent to timer_A, timer_C records the time spent between toto_start_timer and toto_stop_timer, and between titi_start_timer and titi_stop_timer, and timer_E records the time spent between PDI_init and PDI_finalize, including the time spent in the simulation itself.
A mapping, the timers to define and where to output their results. It can also be a sequence of single-key mappings, which has the same meaning:

The events that start and stop the timer named <timer_name>, either:
a mapping with both plugins.timer.<timer_name>.start and plugins.timer.<timer_name>.stop keys,
a scalar, a prefix: the timer is started by the <prefix>_start_timer event and stopped by the <prefix>_stop_timer event,
a sequence of such prefixes, each pair of events starting and stopping the timer.

The prefix can be either a user-defined name, whose events the application has to emit, or one of the following:
pdi, whose events PDI emits in PDI_init and PDI_finalize,
the name of a plugin that emits such events around its own work: decl_hdf5, decl_netcdf, json, pycall, serialize or user_code.
A timer started while already running, or stopped while not running, logs an error and is left unchanged.
Required in the mapping form. A scalar, the name of the event that starts the timer.
Required in the mapping form. A scalar, the name of the event that stops the timer.

Optional. A scalar, where to output the results of the timers: cout (the default) for the standard output, through the logger of the plugin, or the path of a file. The name cout is reserved for standard output so can not be used to name the output file.

The results are appended to the file, one line <timer name>,<seconds> per timer. The plugin uses flock to write sequentially from multiple processes to a single file. This can fail if the underlying filesystem does not support flock, so the standard output is the safer choice.

Optional. The configuration of the logger of the plugin, see plugins.<plugin_name>.logging. This plugin only supports its scalar form, a level, and it then also defines a timer named logging, as for any other key.
